class.name: DampedSpringParameters
class.brief_description: Tuning (response time and damping) for a damped spring, shared by [DampedSpring], [DampedSpring2D], and [DampedSpring3D].
class.description: A [Resource] holding how quickly a damped spring responds ([member time]) and whether it overshoots, settles cleanly, or lags behind ([member damping]). It doesn't hold any spring state itself: no current value, target, or velocity. That state lives on [DampedSpring], [DampedSpring2D], or [DampedSpring3D], which read a [DampedSpringParameters] resource every time their [code]update()[/code] method is called. Because it's a plain, stateless [Resource], one [DampedSpringParameters] can be shared by many spring instances that should all move with the same feel -- for example, every draggable UI element in a menu using the same "snappy" tuning. Use [method setup] to change [member time] and [member damping] together, or set them individually with [member time] and [member damping].

method.name: setup
method.description: Sets [member time] and [member damping] together and recomputes the spring's internal coefficients once. Prefer this over setting [member time] and [member damping] separately when changing both, since each of those setters also triggers its own recomputation.

members.member: How overdamped or underdamped the spring is, clamped to the range [code][-0.9, 0.9][/code]. [code]0.0[/code] is critically damped: the fastest response that doesn't overshoot the target. Positive values are increasingly overdamped, responding more slowly without any overshoot. Negative values are increasingly underdamped: the spring oscillates and overshoots its target, with the magnitude of [member damping] approximating the overshoot as a fraction of the initial displacement (for example, [code]-0.5[/code] overshoots the target by about 50% at its peak).

The furthest the spring's value is allowed to end up from its target, clamped in [code]update()[/code] after each step. Defaults to an effectively unlimited [code]1e9[/code], so it has no effect unless lowered -- useful for capping how far a spring can overshoot or lag behind if [code]target_value[/code] jumps a long way or [code]delta[/code] spikes. Clamped to [code]>= 0.0[/code].

The fastest the spring's internal velocity is allowed to move, clamped in [code]update()[/code] before it's used to advance the value. Defaults to an effectively unlimited [code]1e9[/code], so it has no effect unless lowered -- useful for capping runaway speed from a stiff spring or a large [code]delta[/code]. Clamped to [code]>= 0.0[/code].

How long the spring takes to respond, in seconds. Its precise meaning depends on [member damping]: for a critically damped or overdamped spring ([member damping] [code]>= 0.0[/code]), it's an approximate duration for the spring to settle near its target; for an underdamped spring ([member damping] [code]< 0.0[/code]), it's the time until the spring reaches its first peak overshoot. Clamped to a small positive minimum.
